details.recreationArea: Point of Rocks Ponds  Fishing Site
details.description: These man-made fishing ponds are stocked with trout in the winter and channel catfish during the summer. Please refer to Kansas Dept of Wildlife and Parks for further information regarding licensing, size limit and etc.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.restrictions: Kansas state rules and regulations apply. No swimming allowed.
details.directions: From Elkhart, Kansas, take Highway 27 north, cross the Cimarron River, turn west onto FS 600.3, travel approximately one mile.  Ponds on south side of the road.

properties.name: CIMARRON OVERLOOK
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: A small overlook and parking area which  has scenic views of the Cimarron River valley and interpretive displays about the area's history.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.restrictions: Do not park off constructed roads and parking areas.
details.directions: From Elkhart, Kansas, travel approximately 9 miles north of Elkhart on Hwy 27. The overlook is on the west side Hwy 27 about a mile north of the Cimarron River.

properties.name: MIDDLE SPRING
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: An important watering spot along the Santa Fe National Historic Trail, Middle Springs has picnic tables and interpretative signs about the Santa Fe Trail. A short, easy, nature trail provides visitors a wonderful way to experience this lush riparian habitat and view wildlife.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.restrictions: Closed 10:00 pm to 6:00 am. No camping allowed. Trails are for non-motorized travel only.
details.directions: From Elkhart, Kansas, take Hwy 27 north approximately 7 miles.  Go across the river and turn west on FS 600  Continue approximately 2-3 miles.  Turn north onto FS 653 approximately 1/4 mile turn east on FS 653a.  Enter Middle Springs area across the cattleguard.

properties.name: COTTONWOOD
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Located off Highway 27 south of the Cimarron River, this shady site has many accessible picnic tables as well as a steam tractor display, interpretative signs, and a playground area. Also available are grills and restrooms. The Turkey Trail is nearby.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.hours: Day use only: open 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.
details.restrictions: No horses allowed in picnic area. No wood fires; be aware of any fire restrictions. No camping allowed in picnic area.
details.directions: From Elkhart, take Hwy 27 north approximately 7 miles. Just south of the Cimarron River, turn east onto FSR 700. Take an immediate left (north) turn and continue a short distance into the picnic area.

properties.name: CIMARRON SPORTSMAN CLUB
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

properties.name: MALLARD PONDS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Located east of Cimarron Recreation Area on FS Road 700, these man-made ponds are stocked with fish by the Kansas Dept of Wildlife and Parks. Please refer to Kansas Dept of Wildlife and Parks for further information regarding licensing, size limit and etc.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.restrictions: Kansas state rules and regulations apply. No swimming allowed.
details.directions: From Elkhart, Kansas, take Hwy 27 north approximately 7 miles.  Just before the river, turn east on FS 700.  Continue 5-6 miles.  Pond is on north side of the road.

properties.name: CONESTOGA
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: This Trailhead provides access to the Companion Trail (19 miles) and the Santa Fe National Historic Trail (23 miles). Interpretative signs provide history of the both trails. Accessible horse mounting facilities are available at the trailhead, as well as a restroom and drinking fountain. Both trails are available for a variety of non-motorized travel (horseback riding, hiking, mountain biking) only, providing an opportunity to step back in time and experience what early settlers and traders in the early 1800's may have experienced.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.restrictions: Trails are for non-motorized travel only.
details.directions: From Elkhart, Kansas, take Hwy 56 east to County Road 16 then turn North. Cross the Cimarron River and turn East onto FSR 600; travel approx. 3 miles and turn North onto FSR 615; travel 2 miles to trailhead.

properties.name: MURPHY
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: This Trailhead provides access to the Companion Trail (19 miles) and the Santa Fe National Historic Trail (23 miles). Interpretative signs provide history of both trails. Accessible horse mounting facilities are available. There is also a restroom and a well with handpump. These trails are for non-motorized travel only, giving visitors opportunities to step back in time and see what  "travelling the trail " may have been like.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.restrictions: No camping allowed inside fenced area. Trails are for non-motorized travel only.
details.directions: From Elkhart, Kansas, take Highway 27 north approximately 7 miles, cross the Cimarron River Bridge and turn west onto FSR 600.  Continue west approximately 5-6 miles.  Trailhead is on north side of the road.

properties.name: ATWOOD PONDS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Located in the Cimarron Recreation Area, these four, man-made ponds, were constructed for migratory birds.  There is an accessible fishing pier, covered picnic sites, campground and group picnic area. Trout are stocked in the ponds in the winter and channel catfish are stocked during the summer. Please refer to Kansas Dept of Wildlife and Parks for further information regarding licensing, size limits, etc.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.restrictions: Kansas state rules and regulations apply. No swimming allowed.
details.directions: From Elkhart, Kansas, travel 7 miles north on Hwy 27, turn east (right) on FS 700 and continue 4 miles. Ponds are located in the Cimarron Recreation Area on the north side (left) of the road.

details.restrictions: Closed 10:00 pm to 6:00 am. No camping allowed. Trails are for non-motorized travel only.
details.directions: From Elkhart, Kansas, take Hwy 27 north approximately 7 miles.  Cross the Cimarron River and turn west onto FSR 600.3.  Continue west approximately 3 miles.  Turn south onto FSR 600.3A to Point of Rocks.

properties.name: CIMARRON
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: Located in the Cimarron Recreation Area and surrounded by tall cottonwood trees, this scenic campground has 12 campsites. A great variety of birds provide excellent wildlife viewing opportunities.  The Cimarron Fishing Ponds are nearby.
details.feeDescription:
Overnight Use:
Single Site: $7 per night
details.importantInformation:
Potable water, water hydrants and restrooms are all handicap accessible.

Maps of the Cimarron National Grassland are available at the U. S. Forest Service District Office for $10.00 each or send your request and funds to P. O. Box 300, 242 Highway 56 East, Elkhart, KS 67950. If sending a check, please make out the check to USDA Forest Service.
details.restrictions: Campsites are non-reservable.  Be aware of any fire restrictions. Do not park off constructed roads and parking areas.
details.directions: From Elkhart, Kansas drive north on Highway 27 for 7 miles. Turn right (east) on FS 700 for 4 miles.
details.siteContactNotes:
Year round. Birdwatching is especially good during fall and spring migration seasons. Trout are stocked in the ponds during the winter, and channel catfish are stocked during the summer. 

Winters are moderate, with snow common, but not usually severe. Summers are hot with dry winds.
